title: Piye (Kushite king)
summary: Piye was a Kushite king whose capital was Napata, on the Nile just north of the Fourth Cataract. His expedition into Egypt took Memphis, by one account by seizing its boats and attacking from the east, and drew the submission of the princes of Lower Egypt. His victory stela from Napata is now in the Cairo Museum.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO gives accession in 742 B.C.E.; Livius gives a king-list span of c.747 to c.716 BCE and calls the end date contested. The conquest itself "cannot be dated precisely" (Livius).

when.display: accession 742 BCE; reign c.747–c.716 BCE per Livius

where.modern_name: Gebel Barkal, Karima, Northern State, Sudan (proxy pin for Napata)
where.historical_name: Napata, capital of the Kingdom of Kush

importance.justification: His campaign led to Kushite control of Egypt for almost a century according to EBSCO.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Gebel Barkal

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy: Livius lists Gebel Barkal as a Napatan town and EBSCO places Napata north of the Fourth Cataract; neither gives coordinates. EBSCO says the stela stood at Napata, Livius says it was found at the Amun temple at Gebel Barkal. The dates differ between sources.
